title: Astragaloside IV ameliorates indomethacin-induced intestinal inflammation in rats through inhibiting the activation of NLRP3 inflammasome.
authors: Sun, Qifang; Hu, Mingyue; Yuan, Chengzhi; Ren, Baoping; Zhong, Meiqi; Zhou, Shunhua; Wang, Xiaojuan; Gao, Qing; Zeng, Meiyan; Cai, Xiong; Song, Houpan
one_liner_zh: 该文研究黄芪甲苷对大鼠肠道炎症的缓解作用，涉及NLRP3炎症小体蛋白的分子对接，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: The administration of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) may cause significant intestinal alteration and inflammation and lead to the occurrence of inflammatory diseases resembling duodenal ulcers. Astragaloside IV (AS-IV) is a glycoside of cycloartane-type triterpene isolated from the dried root of Astragalus membranaceus (Fisch.) Bge. (family Fabaceae), and has been used for ameliorating the NSAID-induced inflammation in the small intestine. The present study aimed to investigate the effects of AS-IV on indomethacin (IND)-induced inflammation in the small intestine of rats and its underlying mechanisms. Hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) staining, transmission and scanning electron microscopy were carried out to observe the surface morphology and ultrastructure of the small intestinal mucosa. Immunofluorescence and ELISA tests were employed to detect the expressions of NLRP3, ASC, caspase-1, and NF-kappaB proteins, as well as inflammatory factors IL-1beta and IL-18, to uncover potential molecular mechanisms responsible for mitigating small intestinal inflammation. The results demonstrated that AS-IV significantly decreased the ulcer index, improved the surface morphology and microstructure of the small intestinal mucosa, and increased mucosal blood flow. Molecular docking revealed a strong and stable binding capacity of AS-IV to NLRP3, ASC, caspase-1, and NF-kappaB proteins. Further experimental validation exhibited that AS-IV markedly decreased levels of IL-1beta and IL-18, and inhibited the protein expression of NLRP3, ASC, caspase-1, and NF-kappaB. Our data demonstrate that AS-IV ameliorates IND-induced intestinal inflammation in rats by inhibiting the activation of NLRP3 inflammasome and reducing the release of IL-1beta and IL-18, thereby representing a promising therapy for IND-induced intestinal inflammation.
abstract_zh: 非甾体抗炎药（NSAIDs）的使用可能引起显著的肠道改变和炎症，并导致类似十二指肠溃疡的炎性疾病发生。黄芪甲苷IV（AS-IV）是从黄芪（Astragalus membranaceus (Fisch.) Bge.，豆科）干燥根中分离得到的环阿屯烷型三萜糖苷，已被用于改善NSAIDs引起的小肠炎症。本研究旨在探讨AS-IV对吲哚美辛（IND）诱导的大鼠小肠炎症的影响及其潜在机制。采用苏木精-伊红（H&E）染色、透射和扫描电子显微镜观察小肠黏膜的表面形态和超微结构。通过免疫荧光和ELISA实验检测NLRP3、ASC、caspase-1和NF-kappaB蛋白的表达，以及炎症因子IL-1beta和IL-18的水平，以揭示缓解小肠炎症的潜在分子机制。结果表明，AS-IV显著降低溃疡指数，改善小肠黏膜的表面形态和微结构，并增加黏膜血流量。分子对接显示AS-IV与NLRP3、ASC、caspase-1和NF-kappaB蛋白具有强且稳定的结合能力。进一步的实验验证表明，AS-IV显著降低IL-1beta和IL-18的水平，并抑制NLRP3、ASC、caspase-1和NF-kappaB的蛋白表达。我们的数据表明，AS-IV通过抑制NLRP3炎症小体的激活并减少IL-1beta和IL-18的释放，改善IND诱导的大鼠肠道炎症，从而代表一种有前景的IND诱导肠道炎症治疗策略。
